extracted.intended_audience: cartoonists and humor writers seeking to create Addams-style macabre cartoons
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing single-panel / gag cartoons that fuse horror and domesticity by suggesting the macabre rather than showing it, using visual tone and ordinary behavior for comic inversion. Useful for cartoonists, illustrators, and humor writers aiming for a New Yorker-style macabre sensibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core Approach — defuse fear, infuse playfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: "The goal was never to create fear, but to defuse it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone should disarm horror: aim to make the morbid playful rather than terrifying so the work appeals to readers who prefer daylight to night. Avoid graphic terror; emphasize a light, knowing treatment that neutralizes fear and makes the dark comic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestion over depiction
rubrics_metrics.description: "The suggestion of blood, the suggestion of gore, the suggestion of torture is always there but his cartoons never showed it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imply violent or gruesome elements rather than rendering them explicitly. Let the audience's imagination complete the dark detail — the unseen is often funnier than the seen. Anti-pattern: explicit gore or literal depiction that shuts down the reader's imaginative participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style: morbid + mundane
rubrics_metrics.description: "Addams discovered comic gold at the crossroads of: - The morbid (death, gore, horror) - The mundane (everyday domesticity)"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pair macabre subject matter with banal, domestic settings or routines (family dinner, household chores, holiday traditions). Use ordinary activities as the frame for the grotesque to create a comic dissonance. Scoring note: stronger cartoons make the juxtap feel effortless rather than forced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual techniques and atmosphere
rubrics_metrics.description: Delicate ink wash; atmospheric darkness; Gothic architecture, gnarled trees; family looks "off" but is fully human.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use restrained, atmospheric drawing (delicate washes, heavy atmosphere, gothic motifs) to set a spooky tone without explicit detail. Visual design should suggest a world slightly skewed (gnarled trees, off-kilter architecture) while keeping characters recognizably human. Anti-pattern: cartoony grotesquerie that turns characters into caricature monsters rather than human-but-off.

rubrics_metrics.name: How macabre becomes funny — treatment principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat the morbid AS IF it were ordinary; the family doesn't realize they're spooky; visitors are the ones disturbed; inversion: norm-violating behaviors are this family's norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the aberrant normal within the depicted world so humor arises from the mismatch between the family's perception and outsiders' reactions. Use inversion: behaviors that violate social norms are treated as everyday by protagonists. Example guidance: place the family in a scenario where their casual behavior is shocking to a visitor or viewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric: Is the morbid suggested rather than shown?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the morbid suggested rather than shown?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the cartoon implies dark elements (blood, gore, torture) instead of depicting them literally. Strong examples: silhouettes, off-panel implications, contextual clues; weak examples: explicit gore, graphic detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric: Is the macabre framed as mundane?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the macabre framed as mundane?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the macabre element is embedded in an everyday routine or setting (e.g., holiday, household task) so it reads as ordinary to the characters. The framing should normalize the abnormal to create comic dissonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric: Are the "monstrous" characters going about their day normally?
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the "monstrous" characters going about their day normally?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the 'monstrous' or macabre characters behave as if nothing is wrong — their casual normalcy should be central to the gag. Strong cartoons show characters unconcerned, which highlights outsiders' alarm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric: Is the surrounding world the one disturbed?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the surrounding world the one disturbed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that the narrative perspective makes the external world (visitors, passersby, the reader's assumed norms) react with disturbance, reversing audience expectations. Good work makes the world outside the family's norms the source of discomfort and comedic tension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric: Does the cartoon reward second-look interpretation?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the cartoon reward second-look interpretation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong cartoons contain details or setup that reveal additional darkly comic layers on a second inspection. Examples from the page: family preparing to pour boiling oil on Christmas carolers; a skier bypassing both sides of a tree; cat-shaped silhouette in a cement-mixing tank. Evaluate for clever, compact visual clues that prompt re-interpretation rather than a single, flat gag.
